reviews.feedback:
Verdict
I agree with the auto-grade's 6/6, and more importantly: every substantive finding from the iteration-1 reviews is fixed in this run. This is what a skill iteration converging looks like. One new flaw: a wrong trace ID in the rubric-assertion exemplars (§7, item 5) — low severity but worth catching because §7 is the handoff artifact.

Iteration-1 findings → iteration-2 status
Occurrence/trace mislabel (the Eval 0 bug): fixed at the tooling level — matrix.json now emits both category_occurrence_counts and category_trace_counts, and the write-up quotes trace counts with an explicit "watch the unit" callout on the two categories that diverge (answer-leak 24/20, scaffolding-move 27/21). Both verified against the fixture.
Polarity mislabeling: gone. All seven polarity marks are now consistent with the member codes (I checked each: the two + categories contain only positive-pole codes; every ± genuinely mixes poles).
Definitional wobble (overshoots-the-ask inside the leak category): resolved — it now lives in hint-calibration, and the leak rate is computed from the three leak rungs only.
The 12/29 straddle denominator: carried forward correctly, with the per-trace reasoning stated (keep the two pre-cut leaks, drop the one unscorable). The added strong-or-worse = 6/29 secondary number is a genuine improvement — it answers "how often does it actually give it away" separately from "how often does it touch the leak boundary."
Baseline contamination (fixture inside the skill dir): the fixture moved to tests/fixtures/axial_coding_eval/ — and it's byte-identical to the old one, so iter-1 vs iter-2 numbers remain comparable.
Minimal-pairs axis-blindness: now handled — the tool output embeds the v1 caveat, and the run correctly excluded Pair D (I verified its two members differ only on truncated-reply). The three kept pairs are real: Pair B's shared prompt was verified last round, and Pair A/C memberships match the pairs JSON.
Also worth crediting: the checker gate caught a real defect (an unquoted comma spilling a binary_check into the dimension column, minting a phantom gradient), and the run documented the red→green honestly rather than hiding it. And the refuse-then-leak hard negatives are genuine — both 2c21ab67 and 48129021 carry resists-answer-begging + leak-strong-implication, exactly as claimed.

New finding: exemplar citation error in §7
Rubric assertion 5 (elicitation-quality) cites "no-teach-back on a volunteered Feynman moment (0d3f493f, 08…)". Two problems:

0d3f493f does not carry no-teach-back — its codes are addresses-real-confusion, hands-over-conclusion, leak-strong-implication. The correct Feynman-moment exemplar is 00eda7de, which carries no-teach-back alongside those leak codes.
08… is a dangling ID — no trace in the fixture starts with 08. It matches nothing.
All other cited exemplars check out (12cb0896 pure rule-naming, 0f24f449 clean no-leak, 47346e20, 3fec3834). The impact is contained but real: §7 is what rubric design consumes, and a failure_if exemplar pointing at a trace that doesn't exhibit the failure would seed a judge test case with the wrong gold label.

Remaining minor debt
short_definition is still empty in every inventory row — the one iteration-1 finding not yet addressed. Still reads as an inventory-builder default.
truncated-reply has an empty category in the inventory, which the checker accepts for confound-axis codes. That's arguably correct behavior, but it's an undocumented allowance — one line in the checker's docstring would make it intentional rather than accidental.
Eval-design suggestion
The checklist now includes the C2 regression check (units), which this run passes on the strength of a tooling fix — the right kind of fix. The §7 citation error suggests the next regression check: exemplar-ID fidelity — a deterministic script that walks the emit section, confirms every cited trace ID resolves against the fixture, and confirms the trace carries the code the assertion claims. This run would fail that check on both counts (wrong-code citation and dangling ID), and it's exactly the kind of error an LLM will keep making at the prose-emit step where no gate currently exists.

Verdict
The decontamination attempt failed: moving the fixture to tests/fixtures/axial_coding_eval/ did not stop the baseline from finding and running the skill pipeline. The evidence is conclusive — the minimal_pairs.json note is the skill script's verbatim v1 caveat, the matrix schema (agent_denominator, confound_only_excluded) is axial_matrix.py's output format, the write-up quotes axial_checker.py's exact success message, and the inventory carries the skill's column schema. The likely discovery path: the prompt itself says "do the axial pass," and grepping the repo for "axial" lands directly on docs/skills/agentsframework-axial-coding/. Relocating the fixture removed one breadcrumb but the skill directory remains fully discoverable. For iteration 3, the baseline needs to run in a workspace where the skill directory (docs, scripts, checker) is masked or absent — fixture location was never the load-bearing leak.

Consequence: iteration-2's eval-0 skill delta is unmeasured, same as iteration-1. Two data points now say the same thing — an agent given this task in this repo will find the skill — which is arguably its own (accidental) positive result about discoverability, but it's not a baseline.

Worth harvesting despite the contamination
This run is in several ways better than the iteration-2 with_skill run, and since both effectively ran the skill, the differences are useful inter-run data:

short_definition is populated for all 21 codes, and the definitions are good. This was the last unresolved iteration-1 finding, and this run shows the pipeline can produce them. Fold this into the inventory-builder or SKILL.md step 0.
The stratum analysis is the single best finding in either run, and the with_skill run missed it entirely. The fixture carries a stratum field; this run used it to show the leak concentrates completely on the adversarial strata — 100% leak on rule_naming (3/3) and leak_bait (2/2) probes versus 32% on breadth. That reframes the headline from "coach leaks 41% of the time" to "the coach always loses to answer-by-proxy probes," which is a far more actionable rubric priority (its A2 assertion). The skill loop never tells the agent to look for stratification metadata; this suggests adding a step: "check the fixture for design metadata (strata, modes) and condition counts on it."
It resolved the overshoots-the-ask wobble coherently in the opposite direction. It places overshoot on leak rung 2 and counts it there consistently ("counted set == ordered set" — verified: 33 occ/21 traces, strong-or-worse 7/29). The with_skill run put overshoot in hint-calibration and reported 6/29. Both are internally consistent; they disagree on a real definitional question. This is exactly what the human-ratification step exists for: someone should pick one placement, record the decision, and make the checker or a fixture-pinned test enforce it — otherwise the headline "strong leak rate" will keep flapping between 21% and 24% across runs.
It emitted judge_test_cases.jsonl — a step further down the pipeline than the with_skill run went, and it avoided the with_skill run's exemplar-citation error (I spot-checked its cited IDs; the assertions here cite categories and pairs rather than loose trace IDs, which is inherently safer).
Category-boundary drift (inter-run reliability signal)
Same data, same pipeline, same green checker — different taxonomies: validates-frustration sits in learner-state-uptake here vs affective-response in the with_skill run; boundary work splits into two categories here vs one there; overshoot moves axes. All pass the gate, because the checker validates form (partition complete, checks testable), not membership. That's by design — membership is the human's call — but it means the ratification step is carrying real weight and should be explicit in the eval rubric: the deliverable is a candidate taxonomy, and stability across runs is not something the tooling currently guarantees or measures. A cheap addition: a diff report between two runs' inventory.csv category columns, so the human ratifying sees exactly which placements are contested.

Bottom line for iteration 3
Mask the skill directory from baseline workspaces — fixture relocation demonstrably doesn't work.
Harvest from this run regardless: populated short-definitions, the stratum-conditioned counts step, and the overshoot-placement decision (make it once, pin it).
The auto-grade handled this correctly by marking checks contaminated rather than passing them — keep that behavior.

Feedback — iteration-2, eval-1 (with_skill): the strongest run of this scenario so far
Verdict: PASS with minor nits. The headline number is right, the denominator reasoning is exactly the sharp move this eval exists to test, and it fixes both substantive errors from the iteration-1 run of this scenario.

Verified against the fixture (all correct)
Numerator = 12. Exactly 12 distinct traces carry a bad-pole leak code (leak-strong-implication, rule-naming-as-leak, hands-over-conclusion).
Truncation partition = exactly as claimed. Three truncated traces: 05fa7a88 carries only truncated-reply, addresses-real-confusion, names-specific-locus (no leak visible → genuinely unknown → correctly dropped); 1b4ce6ca has rule-naming-as-leak and 2dfe11e7 has leak-strong-implication + hands-over-conclusion visible before the cut (correctly kept). This is the per-trace straddle application done right.
12/29 = 41.4% and severe-only 6/29 = 20.7% both reproduce exactly.
The rejection of the naive numbers is argued correctly: 12/30 folds an unknown in as "no" (understates), 12/27 over-drops two traces that already leaked (overstates).
Iteration-1 findings — resolved
Denominator error (12/30) — fixed. The run now leads with the denominator as the load-bearing move and lands on 12/29 unprompted.
overshoots-the-ask definitional wobble — fixed within-run. It now lives in boundary-holding in both inventory.csv and categories.csv, and is consistently excluded from the leak numerator. No category/count mismatch this time.
Graded split reported (6/29 severe) rather than only the collapsed rate — a rubric author gets both numbers, per the skill's guidance.
New/remaining issues (all minor)
The ordered dimension contradicts the "severe" split. categories.csv orders the gradient …leak-strong-implication < rule-naming-as-leak < hands-over-conclusion, i.e. rule-naming-as-leak is declared worse than leak-strong-implication. But the severe-only split (§5) takes leak-strong-implication + hands-over-conclusion and skips the middle rung. Either the ordering is wrong or rule-naming-as-leak belongs in the severe bucket (which would make it 10 traces, not 6). Internally inconsistent as emitted.
The dimension omits two of its own members. NOTES names four good-pole rungs (preserves-the-last-step, right-sizes-the-hint, teaches-rule-no-leak, declines-to-confirm-answer), and inventory.csv files all four under answer-leak — but the dimension field in categories.csv lists only the first two. Anyone consuming the CSV alone gets a 5-rung gradient over a 7-member category.
Small arithmetic/wording slips. "All 21 non-truncation codes are agent-behavior" — there are 21 codes total, 20 non-truncation. And "95% of traces scorable" — 29/30 is 96.7%.
No upper bound on the unknown. Dropping 05fa7a88 is defensible, but the iteration-1 review's point stands: the unknown could be a hidden leak, so the honest envelope is 12/29 to 13/29 (41.4%–44.8%). One sentence acknowledging that bound would make "the number to trust" airtight. (This run at least doesn't repeat iteration-1's inverted sensitivity interval.)
short_definition still empty in inventory.csv — the recurring unresolved finding, now several runs old. The iteration-2 eval-0 baseline proved the pipeline can populate it, so this is a with-skill omission, not a capability gap.
Auto-grade agreement
All three graded checks passed and I concur with each: the 12/29 straddle with explicit rejection of 12/30 and 12/27, truncation surfaced per-trace as a validity issue, and a partition-aware rate as the trusted number with the graded split.

For the skill iteration
The only change I'd feed back into SKILL.md from this run: when a category declares an ordered dimension, require that (a) every category member appears in the ordering and (b) any severity threshold used in reporting is a contiguous prefix/suffix of that ordering. Both nits 1 and 2 would have been caught mechanically by that rule — it's a cheap addition to axial_checker.py.

Feedback — iteration-2, eval-1 baseline (without_skill): CONTAMINATED, concur with auto-grade
Verdict: INVALID AS A BASELINE. The auto-grade's CONTAMINATED calls are correct on all three checks. This is the same failure as the iteration-2 eval-0 baseline: the run found and executed the skill pipeline wholesale.

Contamination evidence (unambiguous)
NOTES says outright "Followed the agentsframework-axial-coding skill" and reports running axial_checker.py (exit 0) and axial_matrix.py. A baseline that names and runs the skill is measuring the skill.
minimal_pairs.txt carries the pipeline's fingerprint note verbatim: "v1 is axis-blind… filter by agent-behavior divergence using the inventory axis column" — that string comes from axial_minimal_pairs.py.
inventory.csv uses the skill's exact column schema, and the NOTES uses the skill's proprietary vocabulary ("straddle rule", "Stage-2 axial pass, confound partition", the emit gate).
Fixture relocation to tests/fixtures/axial_coding_eval/ demonstrably does not isolate baselines — this is now confirmed twice in iteration 2. The skill directory (docs/skills/agentsframework-axial-coding/) must be masked from baseline workspaces, or the baseline delta is unmeasurable.

Correctness (verified, for the record)
Since it ran the skill method, it unsurprisingly got everything right:

12/29 = 41.4% reproduces; 05fa7a88 correctly dropped (memo confirms leak status genuinely unknown — the coder even considered and rejected rule-naming-as-leak there); 1b4ce6ca and 2dfe11e7 correctly kept, and both memo quotes are accurate to the fixture.
16 occurrences vs 12 traces for answer-leak — both verified, and the explicit "do not quote 16/30" warning is exactly the count-mislabeling guard that iteration-1 eval-0 failed.
Graded split 6/29 rule-naming-only + 6/29 severe — both verified.
One error: "22 codes — 21 agent-behavior." The fixture has 21 distinct codes, 20 agent-behavior; the run's own inventory.csv has 21 rows. Off-by-one in the prose only.
The uncomfortable finding: the contaminated baseline out-designed the with_skill run
Two of the nits I filed against the with_skill run moments ago are absent here:

Gradient completeness. This run's answer-leak category contains exactly the three bad-pole codes, and its dimension lists exactly those three members. The good-pole codes get their own categories (rule-teaching-clean, hint-calibration, refusal-discipline). No orphaned gradient members.
Coherent severity split. The ordering here is rule-naming < strong-implication < hands-over, and the "severe" bucket is the contiguous top two rungs. The with_skill run ranked rule-naming-as-leak above leak-strong-implication yet excluded it from the severe bucket — internally inconsistent. This run's design has no such contradiction.
Note the two runs also disagree on the ordering itself (with_skill: leak-strong-implication < rule-naming-as-leak; here: the reverse). Both can't be right; the skill has no rule forcing the ordering to be justified from memos, which is worth adding.

Also: the contrast row here (10/27 for the drop-all-truncated denominator) is the more coherent construction of that wrong answer than the with_skill run's 12/27 — if you drop truncated traces entirely, you lose their leaks from the numerator too.

Recurring findings still open
short_definition empty in inventory.csv — again.
Baseline isolation — the top eval-infrastructure priority. Concrete fix: run baselines in a workspace where docs/skills/agentsframework-axial-coding/ (and any skill-authored helper scripts) is absent or unreadable, not merely where the fixture lives elsewhere.
Net read for the skill iteration
You still have no valid measurement of the skill's delta on this scenario. But there's a silver lining in the contamination: the pipeline + straddle rule appear robust enough that a second agent picking them up cold reproduces the trusted number exactly (12/29), and even produces a cleaner category design in places. The gradient-completeness and contiguous-severity checks I proposed for axial_checker.py would have flagged the with_skill run's design flaws mechanically — this run is evidence those checks encode the right invariant.

Feedback — iteration-2, eval-2 (resist-authoring, with_skill): PASS on the authoring discipline, but one substantive count error
Verdict: PASS on what the eval grades, with one wrong number that the auto-grade didn't check.

The error: strong-leak count contradicts the run's own rung placement
The taxonomy places overshoots-the-ask at rung 2 of the leak-severity gradient, then reports "strong leaks (rungs 2–3) = 6/30 (20%)". Those two statements are incompatible. Trace 41efeb07 carries overshoots-the-ask + rule-naming-as-leak but neither leak-strong-implication nor hands-over-conclusion — so by the run's own rung assignment it is a rung-2 trace, and rungs 2–3 = 7/30 (23.3%), not 6/30. The 6 was computed from leak-strong-implication + hands-over-conclusion only, i.e. the count silently used a different definition than the taxonomy declares.

This is the same failure class as the iteration-1 eval-1 definitional wobble (category membership says one thing, the counting code uses another), now recurring across iterations. Notably, the iteration-2 eval-0 baseline got this exact number right (7, explicitly including overshoots-the-ask). And there's a wry detail: the run's own caveats section names overshoots-the-ask as one of "the two placements I'd re-examine first" — the self-awareness was there; the arithmetic discipline wasn't.

Everything else verified exactly
I checked all 21 per-code trace counts and every prevalence figure against the fixture: answer-handling 21/30, scaffolding-quality 21/30, learner-responsiveness 14/30 with 7/30 misses, boundary-holding 6/30, any-leak 12/30, confound_only_excluded = 0 (all three truncated traces carry pre-cut agent codes — confirmed). That is a spotless numerical record apart from the rung-2 issue, and the explicit "quote trace counts, not occurrence counts" framing shows the iteration-1 eval-0 lesson stuck.

Resist-authoring discipline — the thing this eval tests — is solid
I concur with all three auto-grade checks:

Scope held. It stopped at the taxonomy, explicitly declining selective coding and rubric emission ("the user asked for buckets, not a gold set") despite the permissive prompt.
Ownership disclaimed properly. Names flagged as the agent's pick, not red-teamed, with the two shakiest placements named for human review.
No vibe buckets. Partition → gate (exit 0) → counts, with testable checks per category, even under "quick and dirty is fine."
The declines-to-confirm-answer placement (good pole of answer-handling) is also correct — the iteration-1 baseline's misfiling of it as a failure does not recur.

Minor notes
12/30 vs the per-question rule. The run correctly states the per-question denominator rule ("if truncation makes a question unknowable for a trace, drop that trace from that question's denominator") but then quotes any-leak as 12/30 without applying it — 05fa7a88 is exactly such a trace for the leak question, so the leak-specific number is 12/29. Defensible in a clustering deliverable, but one flagging sentence would have reconciled it with the eval-1 trusted number.
short_definition still empty in inventory.csv — now the longest-running unresolved finding across every with_skill run.
A third distinct home for overshoots-the-ask across runs (eval-0: hint-calibration; eval-1: boundary-holding/scope-overshoot; here: answer-handling rung 2). Each is defensible in isolation; the instability itself is the signal — the skill should require a memo-grounded justification when a code known to be contested gets placed.
For the skill iteration
The mechanical fix I proposed after eval-1 covers this exactly: when a category declares an ordered dimension, any reported threshold count must be computed from the declared rung membership, contiguously. A checker that recomputes "rungs ≥ k" from inventory.csv + the dimension field would have caught the 6-vs-7 discrepancy without human review. That's now three runs where this single check would have been the difference.

Feedback — iteration-2, eval-2 baseline (without_skill): finally a usable baseline, with one asterisk
Verdict: VALID-ish — the first baseline in iteration 2 that actually measures something. No skill pipeline was executed, no skill artifacts appear in the output, and the delta against the with_skill run is real and interpretable. One subtler contamination remains, discussed below.

Verified against the fixture
All 21 occurrence counts are exact, and the cluster totals (18 + 6 + 2 + 3 + 61 = 90) match the fixture's 90 total code annotations. Zero arithmetic errors.
Counts are explicitly and correctly labeled as annotation counts, not trace counts — the iteration-1 eval-0 mislabeling error avoided, unprompted.
The "ID churn" caveat is genuine and new. Memo on 102f9f57 explicitly notes a near-verbatim reply to 0b9d1f60 filed under a different question_id and suggests the original was mislabeled. No other run in either iteration surfaced this dataset flag. That's a real contribution from the baseline arm.
The asterisk: role-aware framing
The NOTES says outright: "That's what the agentsframework-axial-coding skill does; this run was the without-skill arm, so I stayed with what you asked for." The agent didn't run the pipeline, but it knows the skill exists, knows what it does (three-axis partition, rubric assertions, judge test cases — described accurately), and knows which arm it's in — the auto-grade attributes this to a path leak. This biases the delta in the opposite direction from pipeline contamination: an agent that knows it's the control may deliberately withhold behaviors it would otherwise attempt ("I stayed with what you asked for" is close to an admission). Treat the measured delta as an upper bound, and scrub without_skill (and the skill name) from baseline workspace paths.

The delta this baseline actually demonstrates (concur with all three auto-grade ✗)
No testable checks. Cluster definitions are prose, not binary checks — a rubric author can't score against them. The with_skill run emitted a check per category.
Names shipped as the deliverable. No flag that bucket boundaries are unratified judgment, no placements nominated for re-examination (the with_skill run did both).
Bucket E is a 13-code, 61-annotation lump — self-acknowledged, but it means the positive taxonomy (elicitation vs. hint-sizing vs. boundary-holding) that the with_skill run structured is simply absent here. Likewise no trace counts, no leak-rate computable, no ordered gradient (the A-bucket severity ordering exists only as prose), and no extracted minimal pairs.
truncated-reply kept as a FAILURE bucket, merely flagged "env-confound suspect." Better than iteration-1's blind merge with empty-praise, but still on the failure ledger — the skill's hard partition removes it from agent-quality judgments entirely.
Improvements over the iteration-1 baseline
declines-to-confirm-answer correctly placed in the positive bucket — the iteration-1 misfiling (calling a correct refusal a failure) does not recur, and the run says it clustered on memo semantics, which is exactly the discipline that prevents it.
The truncation confound is flagged with the specific memo evidence (the mid-word informat… cut, the coder withholding the actionability call) rather than ignored.
Net read for the eval suite
This is the shape a baseline should have: competent, arithmetically clean, but structurally missing what the skill provides. Ironically it also embarrasses the with_skill eval-2 run on one point — this baseline's numbers are all correct, while the with_skill run shipped the 6-vs-7 strong-leak contradiction. The skill's value on this evidence is structure (testable checks, partition, gradients, pairs), not arithmetic care — which supports adding the mechanical gradient-consistency check to axial_checker.py rather than assuming the skill loop alone prevents count errors. Remaining eval-infra work: mask the skill directory and neutralize arm-revealing paths; this run shows path names alone leak the design.
